models.model_label: Asymmetric response to good and bad earnings surprises, all 20 post-formation quarters
models.sample_description: The base sample contains 103,274 firm-quarter observations with I/B/E/S quarterly forecasts, realized EPS and stock prices, plus Compustat growth/value data and CRSP daily returns (1984–1996). Growth portfolio assignments are followed over the next 20 quarters; the all-20-quarter pooled regression contains 1,386,813 firm-quarter/follow-up-quarter observations.
models.method_details: The paper reports regressions but does not identify the underlying estimator for the Table 3 all-20-quarter pooled fit.

dependent_variable.name: R_itτ (fullret)
dependent_variable.definition: Quarterly announcement-to-announcement buy-and-hold stock return with dividends, adjusted using the CRSP value-weighted market index as Table 3 specifies. The fullret interval begins two days after the previous quarter’s earnings announcement and ends the day after the current quarter’s announcement. This model follows the Table 3-specific return definition; the paper’s general description on physical page 7 instead describes a size-matched portfolio adjustment.
dependent_variable.formula: R_itτ = buy-and-hold-with-dividend stock return over the fullret interval − CRSP value-weighted market return over that interval

evidence.quote: Ritτ = the market-adjusted stock return (where the market return is the CRSP value-weighted market index)
for firm i in quarter tτ
Throughout the paper we compute stock returns as buy-hold with-dividend stock returns
We refer to the quarterly return measured over this interval as ‘fullret.’
The first abnormal return measurement interval begins two days after the announcement of earnings for the previous quarter and ends the day after the announcement of earnings for the current quarter
abnormal returns by subtracting the return over the corresponding period on a size-matched portfolio

independent_variables.name: Growth_it
independent_variables.definition: Market-to-book growth quintile assigned to the firm in formation quarter t: 0 is the low-growth quintile and 4 the high-growth quintile. MB is market value of outstanding shares divided by book value of common equity, both measured at quarter end.
independent_variables.formula: Growth_it = quintile(MB_it), coded 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4; MB = market value of outstanding shares / book value of common equity

evidence.quote: Growth portfolios are MB quintiles (low MB = quintile 0, high MB = quintile 4)
growth is measured as the firm’s market-to-book (MB) ratio at the end of quarter t
We measure market-to-book (MB) as the market value of outstanding shares at the end of the quarter divided by book value of common equity at the end of the quarter

research_interest_evidence.description: Table 3 coefficient interpretations and model terms; visually reviewed

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: Growth is the growth-quintile difference for zero-surprise observations, a reference/design term for the primary negative-surprise asymmetry prediction.

evidence.description: Table 3 All 20 quarters row and printed coefficient/t-statistic cells; visually reviewed

missing_fields.reported.standard_error: The table reports adjusted t-statistics, not standard errors.
missing_fields.reported.p_value: No individual coefficient p-value is reported; the table reports only a joint F-test p-value.

independent_variables.name: Good_itτ
independent_variables.definition: Indicator for the sign of the subsequent-quarter forecast error: 1 if FE_itτ > 0 and 0 otherwise. FE is realized quarterly EPS less the consensus analyst EPS forecast, divided by the firm’s stock price at the end of the fiscal quarter; its 1% tails are winsorized.
independent_variables.formula: Good_itτ = 1[FE_itτ > 0], and 0 otherwise; FE_itτ = (realized EPS_itτ − consensus forecast EPS_itτ) / stock price at fiscal-quarter end

evidence.quote: Good itτ = 1 if FE itτ is positive, and 0 otherwise

FE itτ is the forecast error defined as realized EPS for firm i in quarter t + τ minus the corresponding consensus analyst forecast of EPS, deflated by the firm’s stock price at the end of fiscal quarter t + τ
FE is the earnings surprise divided by the stock price at the end of the final month of the fiscal quarter for which earnings is being forecast
We winsorize the 1% tails of this variable to mitigate outlier problems

independent_variables.research_interest_reason: Good is the low-growth positive-surprise increment; the model uses this main effect to define the positive-news reference response.

review_notes: Source-first scope: Table 3 specification (1), all 20 quarters, is the principal full-sample test of the primary prediction that the value/growth return differential is concentrated in negative earnings-surprise observations. Table 2 does not allow an asymmetric response; Table 4 is an alternative forecast-error-magnitude specification that the authors state performs less well; Table 5 return-window analysis is a separate timing prediction.

The Table 3-specific definition of R_itτ as market-adjusted using the CRSP value-weighted market index is used for this fit. The general return description on page 7 says to subtract a size-matched portfolio return; the equation-specific Table 3 definition resolves the selected outcome construction under the source-specificity clarification.

review_notes: Scope: Table 3’s All 20 Quarters column is the central asymmetric-surprise specification testing whether the growth/value return differential is concentrated in negative-surprise quarters. Table 2 does not allow asymmetric responses; Table 4 adds forecast-error magnitude, which the authors say explains the phenomenon less well; Table 5 changes return windows; Table 6 substitutes growth measures; and the later time-series analysis is outside this baseline family.

The return measure is inconsistently described: the general definition on physical PDF page 7 says abnormal returns subtract the corresponding size-matched portfolio return, while Table 3 defines its dependent return as market-adjusted using the CRSP value-weighted market index. The extraction follows Table 3’s model-specific definition and flags the conflict.
The regression estimator is not named; the paper reports adjusted t- and F-statistics for repeated return observations.
results_review_notes: Table 1 summarizes fullret outcome responses and good/bad surprise shares over the same post-formation horizon. Its note specifies decile-based size adjustment, whereas the selected Table 3 fit defines market-adjusted returns using the CRSP value-weighted index; links to the selected model DV are therefore marked unclear.

Figure 4 (physical pages 11–12) plots smoothed mean returns against mean forecast errors for 20 portfolios and has no numerical point labels. No exact numeric portfolio summaries are transcribed from that graph.

The original PDF states that the selected five-year adjusted t-statistics divide by √20 to account for repeated quarterly return observations; the supplied parsed reading says 20. The PDF source governs.
